documents.title: Inhaler + question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Can you send the inhaler again. Also is there a doctor's note thing for work so I can do more inside jobs when it's below freezing? My foreman is ok with it but HR wants paper.

documents.title: RE: Inhaler + question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Inhaler sent. Letter attached recommending indoor or sheltered assignments when temperatures are below freezing because of a circulation condition, through the end of March. Let me know if HR needs different wording.

documents.title: New sores
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Got new sores again, two fingers on my right hand and my left big toe. Started maybe a week or two ago. And now my feet and hands hurt at night in bed, not just walking, which is new. I have the vascular appointment the 29th. Should I come in before?

documents.title: RE: New sores
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Spoke with the doctor. Keep the 5/29 vascular visit; we called their office and you're on their cancellation list. Same wound care as last year. If a sore turns black, gets red and spreading, drains pus, or you get a fever, call us the same day. Please send a photo of the toe.

documents.title: RE: RE: New sores
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Saw the photos - shallow and clean, no sign of infection. Agree with keeping the vascular date. Night pain is a sign this is progressing; we should talk about the cigarettes again after you see them.

documents.title: Vascular surgery follow-up
documents.author: vascular surgery
documents.body:
VASCULAR SURGERY - FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 05/29/2025

37-year-old with thromboangiitis obliterans (diagnosed here 05/2024, arteriogram 06/2024), alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency and ADPKD, back about a year after his first visit. His symptoms have moved on: the hand and foot pain that used to come with walking is now there at rest, worst at night. In cold, the fingers go pale, then blue, then red and throbbing as they warm. Within the last month he has developed painful sores at the tips of two fingers and one toe. Denies fever, weight loss and joint pains.

Meds: albuterol prn; ibuprofen prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: 15 years of smoking; now about 1 pack per day. No alcohol, no drugs.

Exam: small shallow ulcers at the right fingertips and at the tip of the left great toe, clean bases. Hair growth diminished over both lower legs. Dorsalis pedis pulses mildly decreased bilaterally. Radial and ulnar pulses palpable. Digital Allen test abnormal in both hands.

Impression: Buerger disease, progressing to rest pain with new digital ulceration, in the setting of ongoing smoking.

Plan:
1. Smoking cessation once more - the only thing shown to halt this. He was told that continued smoking is likely to lead to digit loss.
2. Wound care as before; protect from cold.
3. No revascularization option per prior arteriogram.
4. Return in one year, sooner for nonhealing ulcer, color change to black, or infection.

NKDA.
Vascular Surgery

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up after vascular.

Night pain in hands and feet most nights, gets up and dangles his feet. Ulcers right 2nd/3rd fingertips and left great toe, doing dressings. Vascular told him straight that he's on the road to losing fingers or toes. Smoking ~1 ppd. He was quieter today. Still says no to varenicline - "I know, I know." Tried cold turkey again in April, three days.

Pain: takes ibuprofen at night a few times a week when it's bad. Reminded about the kidneys and nephrology's advice.

Exam: vitals as charted. Right 2nd and 3rd fingertip ulcers, small, clean, no surrounding erythema. Left great toe tip ulcer, clean, dry. Lower legs with sparse hair. DP faint bilat. Lungs diminished at bases.

A/P
1. Buerger disease with rest pain and new digital ulcers - per vascular; wound care; no infection today.
2. Tobacco use disorder - motivational talk; quitline re-referred; prescription for varenicline offered and declined.
3. ADPKD, AATD/emphysema - specialists in Aug/Oct.
Text photos every 2 weeks until healed.

reports.text: Acceptable efforts. Post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC 0.60. FEV1 67% of predicted.
reports.conclusion: Airflow obstruction; FEV1 67% predicted, down from 70% in 2024.

documents.title: Pulmonology follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
PULMONARY FOLLOW-UP
Visit 08/20/2025

AATD (Pi*ZZ) with basilar emphysema. Buerger disease progressing per vascular. Smoking about 1 ppd.
Symptoms: exertional dyspnea about the same, albuterol most days. No exacerbations.
Spirometry: FEV1/FVC 0.60, FEV1 67% predicted (70% last year, 71% in 2023).
Exam: diminished breath sounds at the bases, no wheeze.

Assessment: slow decline in FEV1 with continued smoking.
Plan: augmentation still deferred until tobacco-free; we would start it promptly once he has quit. Albuterol prn. Return 1 year.
NKDA.
Pulmonology

documents.title: Nephrology follow-up
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
NEPHROLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Visit 10/08/2025

ADPKD. Still smoking; Buerger disease progressed this year per vascular.
Office BP 126/78. Home readings normal.
Creatinine 1.35 (1.3 in 2024, 1.25 in 2023, 1.2 in 2022).
Meds: albuterol prn. Continues some ibuprofen for night pain - reviewed the kidney risk once more.
NKDA.

Assessment: ADPKD with gradually rising creatinine, normotensive.
Plan: unchanged; labs yearly with PCP; return 1 year.
Nephrology
